largestHolders.name: BlackRock Japan Co., Ltd. and its joint holders

structure.note: One class of common stock: 1,287,260,000 shares issued at March 31, 2026, including 134,431,295 treasury shares (Nintendo cancelled 11,430,000 treasury shares on March 31, 2026). No shareholder holds a controlling stake. The register's largest holders are trust-bank and custodian accounts: The Master Trust Bank of Japan (Trust Account) with 16.05% and Custody Bank of Japan (Trust Account) with 5.02%. The largest named non-custodian holder on the register is The Bank of Kyoto with 3.37%. Register percentages exclude treasury shares.

notes: Fiscal year ended March 31, 2026 (Nintendo's 86th fiscal year, the first full year of Nintendo Switch 2). The main source is Nintendo's English 'Annual Report 2026', a translation of its Japanese Annual Securities Report under J-GAAP (the Japanese original prevails), plus the English convocation notice of the 86th AGM (June 2, 2026). Both are on nintendo.co.jp. LEADER: Shigeru Miyamoto is Representative Director and Executive Fellow; relation 'executive' (he was never CEO or chair). He holds 5,000 shares (the notice; the annual report's directors table shows 50 hundred shares). No percentage is disclosed; it is far below 0.01% of the about 1.15 billion shares outstanding, so pctEconomic is null. LARGEST HOLDERS: the three largest disclosed holders that are not trust-bank or custodian nominee accounts. BlackRock's 6.24% comes from a large-volume holding report as of October 31, 2023 that Nintendo quotes in a note to its major-shareholders table, saying it 'could not confirm the actual number of shares held as of March 31, 2026'; that ratio predates the March 2026 cancellation of treasury shares, and is stale. The MUFG and Sumitomo Mitsui Trust group reports quoted in the 2025 report are no longer quoted. The Bank of Kyoto (3.37%, down from 4.19%) and GIC Private Limited (2.10%, account 'C') are from the register at March 31, 2026. The Nomura Trust and Banking Co. (MUFG Bank Retiree Allowance Trust Account, 1.83%) is a trust account and is not listed. DIVIDENDS: the cash-flow line 'Dividends paid' (¥147,858m); the J-GAAP statement shows no separate line for non-controlling interests. BUYBACKS: 'Purchase of treasury shares' ¥99,935m in fiscal 2026 (the line was reclassified out of 'Other, net' this year). STOCK COMP is null: Nintendo grants restricted stock only to Directors and reports only their compensation amounts; no company-wide share-based payment expense is disclosed. GEOGRAPHY: The Americas includes the U.S. (¥790,108m), which is not listed as a separate segment to avoid double counting.

taxes.notes: Fiscal year ended March 31, 2026. Consolidated (Japanese GAAP). R&D: total R&D expenses in general and administrative expenses and manufacturing costs (¥177,892m); R&D within SG&A alone was ¥177,890m.

rnd.notes: Fiscal year ended March 31, 2026. Consolidated (Japanese GAAP). R&D: total R&D expenses in general and administrative expenses and manufacturing costs (¥177,892m); R&D within SG&A alone was ¥177,890m.

paidout.notes: Fiscal year ended March 31, 2026, Japanese GAAP (Annual Securities Report translation). Interest paid, interest and dividends received and income taxes paid are all inside OCF. Time-deposit and securities movements are in investing and are excluded from capex. The FY2025 working-capital distortion (inventory built ahead of the Nintendo Switch 2 launch) has largely unwound: inventories rose only 27,591 in fiscal 2026, while trade receivables rose 74,786 on much higher sales, which lowers OCF and raises paidOut somewhat.

pay.notes: Employees: group head count at March 31, 2026, including part-time workers hired on a regular basis. Payroll is null: the J-GAAP report gives no total personnel expense. It lists only 'Salaries, allowances and bonuses' within selling, general and administrative expenses (¥57,828m), which excludes staff costs in manufacturing and other lines, and an average annual salary for the parent company's employees only; neither is a total of staff costs. As a Japanese filer Nintendo publishes no CEO pay ratio.
